questions.stem: 'Do or Die' (Karenge ya Marenge) was the slogan given by Mahatma Gandhi during which movement?
questions.explanation: Gandhi gave the 'Do or Die' call on 8 August 1942 at Bombay AICC session, hours before the launch of the Quit India Movement (9 Aug 1942). Other Quit India slogans: 'Bharat Chhodo' (Yusuf Meherally coined the phrase 'Quit India'), 'Karo ya Maro' (Hindustani version of Do or Die). Gandhi was arrested 9 Aug; lasted in jail till May 1944.

questions.stem: 'You give me blood, I will give you freedom' was the famous war cry of:
questions.explanation: Subhas Chandra Bose's call — 'Tum mujhe khoon do, main tumhe azadi doonga' — given at a rally on 4 July 1944 in Burma to the Indian National Army (Azad Hind Fauj). Also famously said 'Jai Hind' (now India's national greeting), 'Dilli Chalo'. INA's slogans included 'Itmad, Ittefaq, Qurbani' (Faith, Unity, Sacrifice). His radio broadcasts from Berlin (Azad Hind Radio, 1942) are also iconic. Born 23 January 1897 — observed as 'Parakram Diwas' since 2021.

questions.stem: 'Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it' was declared by:
questions.explanation: Tilak proclaimed this in 1916 during the Home Rule League movement. Tilak's other famous lines: 'The Government should let people boil in misery and despair', 'Lokmanya' (his title — 'one esteemed by the people'). Lal-Bal-Pal trio = Lala Lajpat Rai, Bal Gangadhar Tilak, Bipin Chandra Pal — radical/extremist faction within INC pre-1907. Tilak founded two newspapers — Kesari (Marathi) and The Mahratta (English). Birthplace: Ratnagiri, 23 July 1856.

questions.stem: 'Inquilab Zindabad' — popularised by Bhagat Singh and Batukeshwar Dutt — was originally coined by:
questions.explanation: Hasrat Mohani — Urdu poet and freedom fighter — coined 'Inquilab Zindabad' (Long Live the Revolution) in 1921. Bhagat Singh and B.K. Dutt shouted it after dropping leaflets and a low-intensity bomb in the Central Legislative Assembly on 8 April 1929 — to make 'the deaf hear' (paraphrase of Auguste Vaillant). Bhagat Singh + Sukhdev + Rajguru hanged 23 March 1931 in Lahore. 'Sare Jahan Se Achha' was by Iqbal.

questions.stem: 'Jai Jawan Jai Kisan' was a famous slogan given in 1965 by:
questions.explanation: Shastri coined 'Jai Jawan Jai Kisan' during the 1965 Indo-Pak war + simultaneous food crisis — to hail the soldier defending the border AND the farmer feeding the nation. Vajpayee added 'Jai Vigyan' in 1998 (Pokhran-II). Manmohan Singh once added 'Jai Anusandhan' (research). Modi has since used 'Jai Jawan, Jai Kisan, Jai Vigyan, Jai Anusandhan'. Shastri died in Tashkent 11 Jan 1966 right after signing the Tashkent Agreement; awarded Bharat Ratna posthumously (1966 — first posthumous awardee).

questions.stem: 'Sare Jahan Se Achha Hindostan Hamara' was written by:
questions.explanation: Allama Iqbal wrote the patriotic anthem 'Tarana-e-Hindi' (popularly 'Sare Jahan Se Achha') in 1904. Composed in Urdu, expresses pride in India. Set to tune by Pt. Ravi Shankar at Rakesh Sharma's request when he flew to space in 1984 — Sharma replied 'Sare Jahan Se Achha' when PM Indira Gandhi asked how India looked from space. Iqbal later wrote 'Tarana-e-Milli' supporting the idea of Pakistan. Tagore wrote Jana Gana Mana (1911) and Amar Sonar Bangla (1905, Bangladesh anthem). Bankim wrote Vande Mataram (1875).

questions.stem: 'Garibi Hatao' was the slogan adopted by:
questions.explanation: Indira Gandhi's 1971 Lok Sabha campaign theme — 'Garibi Hatao' (Remove Poverty). Drove an Indira-wave landslide for Congress (R) — 352 seats. Followed by the 1972 Bangladesh Liberation triumph. Modi-era slogans have included 'Sabka Saath Sabka Vikas' (2014), 'Achhe Din' (2014), 'Atmanirbhar Bharat' (2020), 'Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas, Sabka Vishwas, Sabka Prayas' (2021). Older Nehru-era slogan was 'Jai Hind' (Bose-coined, popularised by Nehru).
